title: Socratic checklist — risk of bias & evidence appraisal (评价)
rationale: Step-wise appraisal questions; each signal answer is anchored to source text. Sources are chapter/item-level references.

items.question: Is the risk-of-bias tool matched to each study design (RoB 2 for RCTs, ROBINS-I for non-randomized, QUADAS-2 for DTA)?
items.rationale: Using the wrong instrument invalidates the domain judgments.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.8; QUADAS-2 (Ann Intern Med 2011)

items.question: Is every domain signal question answered with a source-text anchor (quotation or section) rather than a bare judgment?
items.rationale: Appraisal without anchors cannot be audited or reproduced.

items.question: Is the overall risk-of-bias judgment rule (worst-domain vs weighted) pre-specified and applied uniformly?
items.rationale: Ad-hoc aggregation rules let the same domain pattern produce different conclusions.
items.source: RoB 2 guidance (worst-domain default); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.8

items.question: Is the treatment of high-risk studies (exclusion vs sensitivity analysis) pre-specified in the protocol?
items.rationale: Post-hoc exclusion of high-risk studies is a classic bias source.

items.question: Are extraction and appraisal performed by two independent actors with numerical double-checks?
items.rationale: Single-actor extraction and appraisal are the largest sources of data error in reviews.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.5 (data collection); MECIR C43-46

items.question: Are effect estimates, confidence intervals, and sample sizes re-verified against the primary report?
Are retractions, corrections, and expressions of concern re-checked at appraisal time?
items.rationale: Appraising a retracted or corrected record mixes invalid evidence into the review.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.5; Crossref/PubMed records

items.question: Are the domain judgments consistent with the downstream GRADE domains (risk of bias -> certainty)?
items.rationale: Appraisal must feed certainty assessment without double-counting.
items.answer_format: mapping appraisal -> GRADE domain + no-double-count check

items.question: Which appraisal judgment has the lowest confidence, and what would change it?
items.rationale: The weakest judgment is where human review effort should concentrate (uncertainty-aware verification).
items.source: RoB 2 guidance on disagreements; uncertainty-aware verification (Ye et al. ICLR-W 2025)
